A few terms make the plan easier to read
Term Meaning in this roadmap
SLAM VIO / IMU Calibration ROS / bag / replay Pose / frame / reset Health / optional input Simultaneous localization and mapping: estimate camera position while building
a map.
Visual-inertial odometry combines images with an inertial measurement unit:
gyroscope and accelerometer.
Measure camera geometry, camera–IMU alignment, timing offset and sensor
noise.
Robot Operating System passes messages; a bag records them; replay feeds a
saved recording back into software.
Pose is position and orientation; frame defines axes and origin; reset starts a new
estimate.
Health reports valid, lost or old estimates. Optional position information never
owns balance or motor safety.

What a trustworthy raw recording looks like
Raw-data check N2; ROS record/replay N3 follows
Check Required visible result
Exact raw profile Three stages Measured rates Gaps and order Health and stop IR1: Y8 grayscale, 640×480 at 15 Hz; gyroscope 200 Hz; accelerometer 100
Hz.
20 seconds, then 105 seconds, then the mandatory 300-second soak.
Image 14.25–15.75 Hz; gyro 190–210 Hz; accel 95–105 Hz.
Image gaps ≤0.20 s; motion gaps ≤0.05 s; increasing timestamps/frame
numbers; no missing image frames.
All original startup, boundary, content, kernel, power and normal-stop checks
reviewed; raw logs retained.
A short successful take does not replace the five-minute soak.

10/23

Measure how old an estimate is
Estimate age is the time from image capture to the position result being available.
First prove how camera and Pi clocks relate. If that relation is unknown, age is unknown.
Report the median and the 95th/99th percentiles: values below which 50/95/99% of samples fall.
Count every missing input, queued frame, tracking loss and reset alongside CPU, memory, heat and
power.
A fresh status message cannot make an old camera estimate fresh.
11/23

Algorithm comparison: keep one default, test one challenger
Scores from the independent review, checked against the algorithm review; judgments, not Pi benchmarks.
Candidate Demo CPU Motion /100 Decision
ORB-SLAM3 stereo/IMU 5 3 3 68 Default; existing tools
RTAB-Map own motion estimate 3 2 3 68 For an obstacle map
OpenVINS 3 4 3 61 First matched-data challenger
Wheels/body + depth 2 5 2 56 Requires working robot exports
ORB RGB-D 3 3 2 52 New input path needed
Basalt 2 3 3 53 Prove build/adapter benefit
VINS-Fusion 2 3 3 47 Prove port benefit
Kimera-VIO 2 2 3 48 More dependencies; defer
1–5: higher = better fit. RGB-D = color + depth. Total weights: demo 30%, CPU 20%, motion 20%, software
support 15%, navigation 10%, licence 5%.
12/23

What would make us change the algorithm?
Keep ORB-SLAM3 for the first position-estimation trial: build and input work already exist, but live Pi
performance is still open.
If trusted data and correct calibration still miss approved age or continuity limits, spend at most 2–3
days diagnosing; compare OpenVINS on identical retained recordings.
Switch only if the challenger meets the same approved limits and its build, input conversion and
failure behavior are verified.
If the first goal becomes an obstacle/occupancy map, compare RTAB-Map under the complete Pi
workload.
A demonstrated wheel/body interface could make a smaller rolling demo faster; it changes the
deliverable and does not prove camera VIO.
